author: high
claim: In affine coordinates A=(0,0), B=(1,0), C=(0,1), if x=BD/DC, y=CE/EA, and z=AF/FB, then AD, BE, and CF are concurrent if and only if xyz=1.
evidence: Because D,E,F are interior points, x,y,z>0. Division of a segment in a prescribed positive ratio gives D=(1/(1+x),x/(1+x)), E=(0,1/(1+y)), and F=(z/(1+z),0). Thus AD has equation Y=xX, BE has equation X+(1+y)Y=1, and CF has equation (1+z)X+zY=z. The first two lines meet uniquely at P=(1/(1+x(1+y)),x/(1+x(1+y))). Substituting P into the equation of CF gives 1+z+zx=z(1+x+xy), which is equivalent after cancellation to 1=xyz. Hence P lies on CF exactly when xyz=1, proving the equivalence.

glossary.A: first vertex of the nondegenerate triangle
glossary.B: second vertex of the nondegenerate triangle
glossary.C: third vertex of the nondegenerate triangle
glossary.X: first affine coordinate of a variable point
glossary.Y: second affine coordinate of a variable point
glossary.P: the unique intersection point of AD and BE
